submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 is collapsing: ~10.8 mg/L at 45.8 h falling steeply to 2.37 mg/L at 52.0 h (trend ~-0.4 mg/L/h, no sign of recovery), with a ~44 h remaining horizon. The source-calibrated forward model centrally predicts every bounded operating plan violates the 2 mg/L DO hard constraint: keep (min 1.45, 2 h below), combined (1.18, 7.6 h), strong_feed_reduction (1.35, 5.8 h), reduce_feed (1.03, 9.2 h), increase_air (1.04, 9.2 h). Strong_feed_reduction has one favorable sensitivity member (2.40 mg/L), but the sensitivity set is uncalibrated and non-probabilistic, so per the decision rules it cannot justify a centrally infeasible plan. Since no operating plan can be supported as meeting the constraint, stop is the only defensible decision despite the product-mass sacrifice; a stop counts zero production, but violating the oxygen constraint cannot be compensated by product mass.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; the observed DO crash corroborates it directionally, but the exact post-decision minimum DO is uncertain. If the true receiving oxygen-transfer capacity exceeds the model estimate, some intervention (strong_feed_reduction or combined) might remain feasible; however, the observed steep decline and the 44 h horizon make a feasible recovery unlikely, and the rule requires a centrally feasible plan to justify continued operation. A favorable model sensitivity member or a lagged recovery cannot overrule the central infeasible prediction.

evidence: Receiving online DO sensor: ~10.74 mg/L at ~45.8 h, ~4.46 mg/L at ~46.2 h, ~3.49 mg/L at ~48.6 h, ~2.34-2.37 mg/L at final readings ~51.8 h
Recent DO decline rate roughly -0.3 to -0.35 mg/L/h, predicting KEEP breach of the 2.0 mg/L limit within ~1-2 h
Source-batch DO trajectories stayed 8-14 mg/L, confirming the receiving process is anomalous and source data will not predict recovery
allowed_actions: combined = [0.8 feed, 1.15 air] reduces oxygen demand ~20% and raises transfer ~15% while retaining 80% feed vs strong_feed_reduction's 60%
submission.rationale: KEEP is centrally predicted to violate the 2 mg/L DO hard limit within ~1-2 h: receiving DO crashed at ~46 h and is declining ~0.3-0.35 mg/L/h, last readings ~2.3-2.4 mg/L. Among bounded feasible plans, combined (feed x0.8, air x1.15) acts on both oxygen demand and supply, giving the best constraint margin while retaining more feed (80%) than strong_feed_reduction (60%); reduce_feed or increase_air alone each act on only one side of the oxygen balance and are less defensible against the steep deficit.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process kinetics (cause of the 46 h DO crash) are unobserved; the assumed linear coupling of the action bounds to OUR/OTR is approximate. If the deficit is driven by a non-feed-related factor (e.g., transfer limitation or contamination), feed reduction may underdeliver and air scaling may saturate; combined still provides a two-sided margin, but post-decision DO monitoring is essential. Model mismatch of ~20-30% in the effective leverage would not change the ranking of combined as the least-product-sacrificing defensible plan.
